subject: math
title: E-Math trigonometry: ratios and the sine rule

slides.heading: E-Math trigonometry: ratios and the sine rule
bullets: How to name the sides of a right-angled triangle, read the SOH CAH TOA card, and use the sine rule
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we meet the 3-4-5 triangle, build the full SOH CAH TOA card, use the sine rule on a triangle with no right angle, and learn to spot the tangent trap before it costs marks.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Name the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse for an angle and find sin, cos and tan
Use the sine rule to find an unknown side in any triangle
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud slowly and tell the class: keep these in mind, because our exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these two things.

slides.heading: The triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5
bullets: A right-angled triangle has short sides 3 and 4 - what is the longest side?
Three ratios hide in this one triangle: can you find all three?
slides.notes: Ask for a show of hands and take two or three guesses without judging them yet; say: hold on to your idea, because naming the sides correctly is the key to the whole lesson.

slides.heading: Naming the sides comes first
bullets: The hypotenuse is the longest side, across from the right angle
The opposite side is across from the angle theta; the adjacent side sits next to theta
Every ratio is two of these sides divided: sine, cosine and tangent each pick a different pair
slides.notes: Say this part slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: the ratio names only mean something once you have named the sides from the angle you are working with.

slides.heading: Meet the 3-4-5 triangle
bullets: Opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, hypotenuse = 5
Sine is opposite over hypotenuse: sin theta = 3/5 = 0.6
slides.notes: Point at the animation and narrate what is happening: watch the dot walk the three sides so you can name each one, then watch the sine equation appear - opposite over hypotenuse.

slides.heading: Cosine and tangent join the card
bullets: Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse: cos theta = 4/5 = 0.8
Tangent is opposite over adjacent: tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75 - read the card as SOH CAH TOA
slides.notes: Tell them to watch the card fill in line by line: SOH for sine, CAH for cosine, TOA for tangent. Point at the tangent line longest - it is the one the trap targets.

slides.heading: The sine rule for any triangle
bullets: The sine rule links each side with the sine of its opposite angle: a / sin A = b / sin B
With a = 4, A = 30 degrees and B = 60 degrees, b comes out to about 6.93
slides.notes: Name the shift out loud: no right angle here, so SOH CAH TOA cannot help directly - the sine rule pairs each side with its opposite angle instead.

slides.heading: A common mistake: do not flip tangent
bullets: Tempting wrong turn: tan = adjacent / opposite.
The flipped ratio gives 4/3 = 1.33, taller than the whole - TOA says tan is opposite over adjacent, 3/4 = 0.75
slides.notes: Name the trap out loud before anyone falls into it: opposite and adjacent swap places under pressure, so always read TOA before writing the tangent ratio.

slides.heading: Worked example: finding side b with the sine rule
bullets: Step 1: write the rule with the known pair: 4 / sin 30 degrees = b / sin 60 degrees
Step 2: b = (4 x 0.8660) / 0.5, so b is about 6.93
slides.notes: Talk through the two steps slowly and name each one as you write it; say: notice the known side and its opposite angle stay paired together in the rule.

slides.heading: Your turn: ratios, then correct
bullets: For the 3-4-5 triangle, write down sin theta, cos theta and tan theta from the side names
Careful - a classmate writes tan = adjacent / opposite. Explain to them why that is wrong, using TOA and the 3-4-5 triangle
slides.notes: Give pairs two minutes, then cold-call one pair and press them on the trap: if tangent really were adjacent over opposite, would tan theta be 3/4 or 4/3 for this triangle?

slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
bullets: Find a side with the sine rule, showing the paired substitution
Explain why this claim is wrong: tan = adjacent / opposite.
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the words opposite over adjacent in your last answer - if you can explain why TOA fixes the tangent, you have cracked today's lesson.
